skill.name: ai-automation-workflows
skill.description: Design AI automation workflows with inference.sh, bash, cron, webhooks, and Python examples for repeatable model tasks.
skill.summary: Create reusable AI automation patterns for batch jobs, pipelines, schedules, monitoring, and content generation.
skill.author: inference-sh-9

security_audit.summary: Most fenced-code, shebang, and formatting matches are false positives caused by Markdown examples. Real risks remain: a pipe-to-shell installer, cron persistence guidance, a dynamic command wrapper, local file disclosure to external AI services, and unredacted webhook alerts.

remediation.issue: Remote install command pipes a downloaded script directly to sh.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell with manual download, checksum verification, and explicit user confirmation before execution.
Add owner, permission, review, and disable instructions for each scheduled job.

remediation.issue: The data processing template sends local file contents to hosted AI models.
remediation.suggestion: Add data classification, redaction, and consent checks before sending file contents to external services.

remediation.issue: Webhook alerting sends raw errors and command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Redact secrets and use configurable, authenticated webhook destinations with an allowlist.

content.value_statement: AI automation often becomes fragile when scripts mix models, schedules, and retries without structure. This skill provides reusable workflow patterns for batch jobs, pipelines, monitoring, and scheduled generation.
actual_capabilities: Shows batch processing with repeated inference.sh CLI calls.
Outlines sequential pipelines for research, writing, image generation, and social posts.
Provides examples for parallel jobs, retries, fallback models, and conditional branches.
Includes cron-based scheduling patterns for daily and weekly workflows.
Shows logging, alerting, and Python subprocess automation for inference.sh.
limitations: Examples rely on inference.sh CLI access and configured credentials.
The skill provides workflow templates, not a managed scheduler or runtime.
Sample scripts need review before handling private or regulated data.
Cron, webhooks, and install commands require local security controls.

use_cases.title: Plan Recurring Content Workflows
use_cases.description: Create repeatable pipelines for images, captions, articles, and social posts with clear outputs and retry behavior.

use_cases.title: Process Text Data with AI
use_cases.description: Design scheduled file processing that summarizes documents, extracts insights, and writes structured results for later review.

use_cases.title: Harden AI Batch Jobs
use_cases.description: Add logging, alerts, rate limits, fallbacks, and idempotent outputs to scripted model workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Begin Batch Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a beginner batch workflow for [items]. Include input format, model choice, rate limit delay, and output naming.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Sequential Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a pipeline that turns [topic] into [deliverables]. Include each AI call, dependencies, failure handling, and outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Add Scheduling and Monitoring
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to convert [workflow] into a scheduled job. Include schedule, logs, alerts, retries, and safe shutdown steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Production Workflow Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design an advanced AI automation system for [business process]. Include model routing, privacy checks, idempotency, observability, and rollback steps.

best_practices: Review every generated script before running it on a workstation or server.
Redact secrets and private data before sending prompts to hosted AI services.
Use logs, retries, and idempotent outputs for every scheduled workflow.
anti_patterns: Piping remote install scripts directly into a shell without verification.
Running cron jobs without owners, disable steps, or log rotation.
Sending raw files, errors, or command arguments to webhooks without redaction.

faq.question: Does this skill run workflows by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and prompts. You must configure scripts, credentials, schedules, and execution permissions.

faq.question: Which tools does it target?
faq.answer: It targets the inference.sh CLI, bash scripts, cron scheduling, webhooks, and a Python subprocess example.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code according to its marketplace metadata.

faq.question: Does it require an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: The examples assume the inference.sh CLI is installed and authenticated before workflow commands run.

faq.question: Can it process sensitive data?
faq.answer: It can describe data workflows, but sensitive data needs redaction, approval, and service review before external model calls.

faq.question: Is it safe to copy the shell examples directly?
faq.answer: No. Review paths, permissions, secrets, install commands, and network destinations before running any example.
